title: Principles relating to processing of personal data
text: Personal data shall be processed lawfully, fairly, and transparently (lawfulness, fairness, transparency); collected for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes (purpose limitation); adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary (data minimisation); accurate and kept up to date (accuracy); kept in a form permitting identification no longer than necessary (storage limitation); and processed with appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage, using appropriate technical or organisational measures (integrity and confidentiality). The controller is responsible for, and able to demonstrate, compliance (accountability).

title: Responsibility of the controller
text: The controller shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and to be able to demonstrate that processing is performed in accordance with the GDPR, taking into account the nature, scope, context, and purposes of processing and the risks to data subjects. These measures shall be reviewed and updated where necessary.

title: Data protection by design and by default
text: The controller shall implement technical and organisational measures -- both at the time of determining processing means and of the processing itself -- designed to implement data protection principles and integrate necessary safeguards (data protection by design). By default, only data necessary for each specific purpose are processed, with their accessibility, amount, period of storage, and accessibility restricted by default (data protection by default). Certification mechanisms can be used to demonstrate compliance.

title: Records of processing activities
text: Each controller and, where applicable, their representative shall maintain a record of processing activities: the purposes of processing, categories of data subjects and personal data, categories of recipients, transfers to third countries, envisaged retention periods, and a general description of the technical and organisational security measures. Controllers and processors are to cooperate on an ongoing basis in fulfilling this obligation.

title: Security of processing
text: Taking into account the state of the art, costs, nature, scope, context, and purposes of processing and associated risks, the controller and processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk: pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data; the ability to ensure ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability, and resilience of processing systems; the ability to restore availability and access in a timely manner in the event of an incident; and a process for regularly testing, assessing, and evaluating the effectiveness of the measures. Compliance with an approved code of conduct or certification may be used as an element demonstrating compliance.

title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
text: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall notify the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons. The notification must describe the nature of the breach, categories and number of data subjects, measures taken or proposed, and consequences. Processors must notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a breach.

title: Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject
text: When a personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall communicate the breach to the data subject without undue delay, in clear and plain language, describing the nature of the breach, the recommended measures to mitigate adverse effects, and who to contact. It is not required if appropriate measures (e.g., encryption) render the data unintelligible, or later measures eliminate the high risk.

title: Data protection impact assessment
text: A data protection impact assessment (DPIA) is required where processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, in particular using new technologies, large-scale processing, or systematic monitoring. The DPIA shall describe the processing and purposes, assess necessity and proportionality, assess risks to data subjects, and set out measures to address risks and demonstrate compliance, including safeguards, security measures, and mechanisms to protect personal data.

title: Designation of the data protection officer
text: A data protection officer (DPO) shall be designated where processing is carried out by a public authority, where core activities require regular and systematic monitoring of data subjects on a large scale, or where core activities consist of large-scale processing of special categories of data or data relating to criminal convictions. The DPO may be a staff member or service provider, and must be provided with resources to perform duties, must not be instructed in relation to those duties, and must not be dismissed or penalised for performing them.

title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
text: Where a transfer of personal data to a third country or international organisation does not take place on the basis of an adequacy decision, it may take place only if appropriate safeguards are provided and enforceable rights and effective legal remedies are available, for example binding corporate rules (BCRs), standard contractual clauses (SCCs), or an approved code of conduct.

title: Processing in the context of employment
text: Member States may provide by law or collective agreements for more specific rules to ensure the protection of the rights and freedoms of employees' personal data in the employment context, including processing for recruitment, performance of the contract, management of the working relationship, and safety at work.
